newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks boycott would be serious - SBC's Ospel.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks boycott would be serious - SBC's Ospel.

text.p: Marcel Ospel, chief executive of Swiss Bank Corp. (SBC), said a Jewish-led boycott of Swiss banks would have serious consequences, but he saw no signs of any conspiracy against the banks.

Ospel, the most prominent Swiss banker so far to address the issue of dormant accounts left by Jewish victims of the Nazi Holocaust, added that recent statements had eased his concern about a possible boycott.

"Threats of a boycott are very uncomfortable for us. And if a boycott were to come about, de facto or de jure, then it would be serious, without a doubt," Ospel said in an interview with Swiss financial bi-weekly Finanz und Wirtschaft.
It was released ahead of publication on Saturday.

"But in judging the situation, there are three reactions that give me reason for confidence," Ospel added, referring to the response of the Swiss Jewish Federation, U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato and the Israeli foreign minister.
All three have clearly spoken out against such a boycott, Ospel added.

The threat of a boycott of Swiss banks has been raised several times in recent months as a way to force the banks to speed up the hunt for Holocaust accounts or force Berne to set up a compensation fund for heirs of Holocaust victims.
Earlier this week Swiss bank shares lost ground in selling that traders blamed in part on renewed talk of a Jewish boycott.

But Ospel said the recent fall in the share prices of Switzerland's three Big Banks was a technical reaction to recent gains and was wrongly was linked with the threats of a boycott, even if there was a danger of such a move initially.
Asked whether he thought there was conspiracy behind the attacks on Swiss banks, Ospel said he saw no such signs.
"We have absolutely no indications of that," Ospel said.
